title: The Silence Clause in Médecins Sans Frontières' First Charter
conflicts: The slate's premise (founded to speak out) conflicts with MSF's own archive: the December 1971 charter and statutes bound members to discretion, and former MSF president Rony Brauman calls the speaking-out origin a myth that took hold in the late 1970s. MSF Ireland's history page still says Récamier and Kouchner openly criticised Nigeria and the Red Cross; the story attributes that to MSF and notes a historian's contrary finding. Founder counts differ (12 signatories of the statutes, 13 in MSF South Asia's list, 15 doctors at the 20 December meeting per Tonus); dates differ (20 versus 22 December); the story gives both dates and no founder total.
notes: Several founders named, doctors and journalists, not Kouchner alone. Brauman's article is cited in its French edition on icrc.org (loads, but as a compressed PDF it does not register names for the checker). The Desgrandchamps article is known only through Brauman (cairn.info blocks automated requests).
